Other ways to earn Wyndham points - Book Wyndham Rewards travel bundles: When you book your hotel, flights, car rental and activities through Wyndham Rewards, you can earn up to 10 points per dollar spent on qualifying hotel stays and activities and 1 point per dollar spent on all other travel reservations. - Buy Wyndham points: You can buy up to 100,000 points per calendar year for your account. Standard points pricing is 1.3 cents each, but you'll sometimes see points on sale for as much as a 100% bonus, which brings the purchase cost down to 0.65 cents per point. - Dine Out with Wyndham Rewards: You can earn up to 5 Wyndham points per dollar spent on dine-in and takeout orders when you use a card you've linked to the Dine Out with Wyndham Rewards program to pay at a participating restaurant. - Host a meeting or event: Planners earn 1 point per dollar spent on qualifying group, meeting and event spending, including rooms when you book 10 or more rooms on at least one night of your event, event space cost and event food-and-beverage charges. However, note that not all properties participate in the Groups, Meetings & Events program. - Book rental cars: Earn 2 Wyndham points per dollar spent and enjoy discounted rates when you book an Alamo, Enterprise or National rental car at a qualifying rate through the Wyndham Hotels & Resorts website. Note that you won't earn rental car rewards on your rental. - Take surveys: You can earn Wyndham points by taking surveys through the Opinion Rewards Panel or e-Rewards. - Buy through Ticketmaster: If you link your Wyndham Rewards account to your Ticketmaster account, you'll earn 1 Wyndham point per dollar spent on the base ticket price for eligible purchases made on the official Ticketmaster website while logged into your Ticketmaster account (up to a maximum of 25,000 Wyndham Rewards points per calendar year; Wyndham Rewards Insider members earn 2 points per dollar spent). How to redeem Wyndham Rewards points There are several ways to redeem Wyndham Rewards points. TPG's September 2026 valuations have Wyndham Rewards points at 0.7 cents each, so you'll typically want to get at least 0.7 cents per Wyndham point on redemptions. Redeem for free nights The best way to use your Wyndham Rewards points is usually for award nights at participating hotels, participating Caesars Rewards properties, participating destinations and Cottages.com properties. As of Sept. 15, Wyndham has an award chart with four different pricing tiers: 5,000, 15,000, 30,000 and 45,000 points per night. You'll find 1,788 Wyndham hotels and resorts at the 5,000-point tier. Many of these properties belong to budget-friendly brands and can be found along major expressways or in off-the-beaten-path destinations. However, nine Club Wyndham vacation properties can be booked for just 5,000 points per night, including the Club Wyndham Cypress Palms in Florida and the Club Wyndham Legacy Golf Resort in Arizona. You'll also find some full-service properties in this tier, including the Palma Resort Phu Quoc, Trademark Collection by Wyndham in Vietnam and the Wyndham Corfu Acharavi in Greece. At the 15,000-point tier, you'll find 3,665 properties. Some of our favorite sweet spots at the 15,000-point tier are the Grand Decameron Panama, A Trademark All Inclusive Resort in Panama; the Viva Heavens by Wyndham, A Trademark All Inclusive in the Dominican Republic; the Wyndham Grand Athens in Greece; and the WorldMark Steamboat Springs in Colorado. Moving on to the 30,000-point tier, you'll find 2,882 properties. These properties are usually upscale hotels, but some are simply properties in appealing destinations. Some of our favorites include the Kunuku Resort All Inclusive Curacao, Trademark by Wyndham; the Club Wyndham Midtown 45 in New York City; and the Margaritaville Vacation Club — St. Thomas in the U.S. Virgin Islands. And 68 properties are at the 45,000-point tier. These properties include the Wyndham Grand Clearwater Beach in Florida, the Esplendor by Wyndham Isla Mujeres Boutique All Inclusive in Mexico and the Wyndham Alltra Punta Cana All Inclusive Resort in the Dominican Republic. Interestingly, you can book multibedroom accommodations at nine Wyndham Vacation Club properties for just 5,000 points per bedroom, per night. As such, a two-bedroom villa at select Wyndham Vacation Club properties could cost just 10,000 points per night. You can also book Cottages.com properties in the U.K. for 15,000 points per bedroom, per night, though you'll need to call to book. When booking free night awards with their account, select Wyndham cardholders get a redemption discount: - 10% redemption discount: Wyndham Rewards Earner Card and Wyndham Rewards Earner Plus Card - 20% redemption discount: Wyndham Rewards Earner Business Card - 25% redemption discount: Wyndham Rewards Earner Premier Card You'll need the full standard amount of points in your account to book an award via the Wyndham website or app, even if you have access to a redemption discount. However, cardholders can call to book an award stay if they don't have enough points to cover the standard award cost but do have enough for the discounted award cost. Finally, you can also book Points + Cash nights for stays at participating hotels, participating Caesars Rewards properties and participating destinations. Specifically, here's how the award costs break down for Points + Cash stays: - 5,000-point property: Starting at 500 points plus cash - 15,000-point property: Starting at 1,500 points plus cash - 30,000-point property: Starting at 3,000 points plus cash - 45,000-point property: Starting at 4,500 points plus cash Redeem for Wyndham Rewards Experiences You can bid and redeem Wyndham points for experiences via the Wyndham Rewards Experiences platform. The options change frequently but often include VIP tickets to performances and sporting events. They also occasionally include special meet-and-greets with celebrities. Related: 8 of the most exclusive travel experiences you can book with points and miles Other ways to redeem Wyndham points - Partner travel currency: You can redeem Wyndham points for points or miles with select travel partners, including United MileagePlus, Air Canada Aeroplan and Avianca Lifemiles. Doing so will usually provide poor value compared to award nights, though. - AARP membership: You can redeem 3,000 Wyndham points to join AARP or renew your membership for one year. This typically costs $20 per year, so you'll get 0.67 cents per point. - Retail gift cards: You can redeem Wyndham points for gift cards. Most types of retail gift cards cost 3,000 points for a $10 card, 7,500 points for a $25 card, 14,000 points for a $50 card and 27,000 points for a $100 card. This means you'd get between 0.33 and 0.37 cents per point when redeeming for most gift cards. - Visa gift cards: If you prefer to cash out your Wyndham points, you can redeem them for Visa prepaid cards. The cards expire after six months and cost 8,000 points for a $25 card, 15,000 points for a $50 card and 29,000 points for a $100 card. This means you'd get between 0.31 and 0.34 cents per point. - Points Payback: Eligible Wyndham cardholders can redeem points for statement credits toward purchases made within the previous 90 days. - Merchandise: You can redeem Wyndham points for a wide range of merchandise. For example, Bose QuietComfort Earbud Headphones would cost 61,122 Wyndham points. With a comparable paid rate of $149 through Amazon, you'd get 0.24 cents per point. - Charitable donations: You can donate as few as 500 Wyndham points to a selection of charities. - Airline tickets, car rentals and private transportation: You can also redeem Wyndham points to book airline tickets, rental cars and private transportation. Most redemption options in this section offer well under TPG's valuation of Wyndham points, as you'll usually get much better value when you use your Wyndham points for award nights. Do Wyndham Rewards points expire? Wyndham Rewards points generally expire four years after they're posted to your account. However, your points could expire sooner if 18 consecutive months pass without any earning, redeeming or transferring activity for your Wyndham points. One exception to the standard Wyndham points expiration rules is that points earned by a Wyndham Rewards Earner Premier Card member won't expire as long as the card account is open and in good standing. However, if you close your card or your account is no longer considered in good standing, your points will become subject to the standard expiration rules again. Related: How to keep your points and miles from expiring Wyndham Rewards pros and cons If you're considering whether to use the Wyndham Rewards program, here's a summary of the pros: - Simple fixed award chart with four redemption tiers - Large footprint of around 8,400 hotels in about 100 countries - Relatively easy to earn points, including a minimum of 1,000 points on most qualifying stays - Multiple transferable rewards partners, including Bilt, Capital One, Chase, Citi and Wells Fargo - Elite status is easy to get through Wyndham cards and status matches - Eligible Wyndham cardholders get a 10% to 25% discount on free night awards But the program isn't perfect. Here's a summary of the cons: - Elite benefits are weak compared with major competitors like Hilton, Marriott and Hyatt. - Even Diamond status doesn't include perks like complimentary breakfast and lounge access. - Many nonhotel redemptions offer significantly less value than award stays. - Points usually expire after four years, or sooner if your account is inactive for 18 months. Wyndham Rewards won't be the best fit for every traveler. But its fixed award chart, broad hotel footprint, multiple transfer partners and accessible elite status can still make the program useful, particularly when cash rates are high or you find a compelling redemption opportunity. Frequently asked questions Wyndham Rewards is free to join, and even entry-level members get benefits like free Wi-Fi and access to member rates. Wyndham Rewards points generally expire four years after they are posted to your account. However, you could lose your points sooner if you go 18 consecutive months without earning, redeeming or transferring points. TPG values Wyndham Rewards points at 0.7 cents each as of September 2026. However, you may get significantly more or less value depending on how you redeem your points. As of Sept. 15, 2026, Wyndham Rewards free nights cost 5,000, 15,000, 30,000 or 45,000 points per bedroom per night. Some eligible Wyndham cardholders get a 10% to 25% discount when redeeming points for free nights. Wyndham Rewards free nights and Points + Cash nights both count as qualifying nights toward elite status. However, if you book multiple rooms or units for the same night, only the one you stay in counts as a qualifying night. U.S. travelers can transfer Bilt Points, Capital One miles, Chase Ultimate Rewards points, Citi ThankYou Rewards points and Wells Fargo Rewards points to Wyndham Rewards. Transfer ratios vary by program, though, and transferring to Wyndham won't always provide the best value for your transferable rewards.

item.title: Ultimate guide to the Hilton Honors loyalty program
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.01
Ultimate guide to the Hilton Honors loyalty program Editor's Note - Hilton Honors is one of the largest hotel loyalty programs in the world, with more than 9,000 properties. - While not the most valuable hotel points, Hilton points are easy to earn and redeem, with frequent promotions, bonuses and redemption options beyond stays. - Hilton Diamond status can be yours with the right credit card. Hilton Honors is one of the largest hotel loyalty programs, with over 9,000 participating properties across 27 brands. I appreciate that the program offers excellent opportunities to earn Hilton points, valuable cobranded credit cards and multiple pathways to secure elite status. Although Hilton Honors isn't my primary hotel loyalty program, I maintain Hilton elite status through a cobranded credit card and stay at Hilton properties at least quarterly to maximize the up to $50 per quarter Hilton statement credit available through The Business Platinum Card® from American Express (enrollment is required; separate Hilton for Business enrollment is also required). So, whether you stay at Hilton properties weekly or annually, here's what you should know about the Hilton Honors program. What is Hilton Honors? Hilton Honors is the hotel loyalty program for Hilton hotels and resorts. It provides benefits and earnings on eligible stays at 27 Hilton brands, from full-service luxury brands like Waldorf Astoria and Conrad to select-service brands like Hilton Garden Inn and Hampton by Hilton. Hilton also launched its Select by Hilton collection earlier this year, adding Yotel as the collection's first brand. The Hilton Honors program offers various ways to earn and redeem Hilton points, too, including many options beyond hotel stays. One of these options is Hilton Honors Adventures, which lets you earn and redeem points for adventure-driven travel experiences. Initial partners for Hilton Honors Adventures are AutoCamp and Explora Journeys. When you book directly with Hilton, you'll earn points and benefits based on your membership tier. For the rest of this article, I'll assume you book through Hilton (not an online travel agency or other method) when discussing benefits and earnings. Related: The 22 best Hilton hotels in the world Hilton Honors membership tiers You'll progress up the Hilton Honors membership tiers as you stay at Hilton properties each calendar year. Once you've earned a specific membership tier, you'll enjoy its benefits for the rest of the calendar year in which you earned it and for the entire next calendar year. You can also snag Hilton Honors elite status through a status match or as a cardmember of select American Express cards. Comparison of Hilton Honors membership tiers | Membership tier | Qualification requirements per calendar year | Key benefits | Which credit cards give automatic access to this membership tier? | |---|---|---|---| | Member | None | Discounted rates, waived resort fees on award stays and Wi-Fi access | None | | Silver | Stay four times, stay for 10 nights or spend $2,500 | A 20% bonus on base points earned through stays and the fifth-night-free benefit on standard reward stays | | | Gold | Stay 15 times, stay for 25 nights or spend $6,000 | An 80% bonus on base points earned through stays, a choice of a My Way on-property benefit on each stay and space-available room upgrades | | | Diamond | Stay 25 times, stay for 50 nights or spend $11,500 | A 100% bonus on base points earned through stays, executive lounge access and premium Wi-Fi access | | | Diamond Reserve | Stay 40 times or 80 nights and spend $18,000 | A 120% bonus on base points earned through stays, 4 p.m. guaranteed late checkout, premium club access and one confirmable upgrade reward | None | Check out the following sections to learn more about each of these Hilton Honors membership tiers and other benefits you can enjoy on Hilton Honors stays. Hilton Honors member Once you join the Hilton Honors program, you'll be a member. The primary benefits of being a Hilton Honors member are: - Access to book the Hilton Honors discount rate - Waived resort fees when you pay for your stay using solely points or a promotional free night reward - The ability to choose your room from available rooms up to 24 hours before check-in - Free Wi-Fi throughout the hotel - The ability to earn points on stays - Late checkout, upon request and subject to availability It's free to join the Hilton Honors program, so you might as well join now if you aren't already a member. Hilton Honors Silver You'll earn Hilton Honors Silver status after you stay four times, stay for 10 nights or spend $2,500 in a calendar year. Eligible spending includes room rates and charges billed to your room (such as spa, dining and other incidental charges) from bookings made directly with Hilton or approved channels. The primary benefits of Hilton Silver status include: - A 20% bonus on base points earned through stays - Two complimentary bottles of water per stay at select hotels - A fifth night free on standard reward stays of five consecutive nights or more (up to four free nights per stay and only when you book solely with points) - Access to a spa discount of 15% on a single treatment when staying at Hilton all-inclusive properties with a spa You'll also enjoy Hilton Silver status as a cardmember benefit of the Hilton Honors American Express Card. Unfortunately, Hilton Honors eliminated rollover nights beginning in 2026, although qualifying nights rolled over from 2025 can still count toward 2026 status. Hilton Honors Gold You'll earn Hilton Honors Gold status after you stay 15 times, stay for 25 nights or spend $6,000 in a calendar year. The primary benefits of Hilton Gold status include: - An 80% bonus on base points earned through stays - A choice of a My Way on-property benefit on each stay (which may include the option to select a daily food-and-beverage credit or continental breakfast) - Space-available room upgrades to preferred rooms (including up to executive floor room types) at select brands and properties You'll also get Hilton Gold status as a cardmember benefit of the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass Card, the Hilton Honors American Express Business Card, the American Express Platinum Card and the Business Platinum Card from American Express (enrollment may be required). You can also earn Gold status through the end of the next calendar year if you spend $20,000 on eligible purchases on the Hilton Honors American Express Card within a calendar year. Related: Which Hilton hotels offer free breakfast? A guide to brand and elite benefits Hilton Honors Diamond You'll earn Hilton Honors Diamond status after you stay 25 times, stay for 50 nights or spend $11,500 in a calendar year. The primary benefits of Hilton Diamond status include: - A 100% bonus on base points earned through stays - Executive lounge access when available - Premium Wi-Fi access during stays at select brands - Space-available room upgrades to preferred rooms (including up to junior, standard or one-bedroom suites) at select brands and properties You can also obtain Hilton Diamond status as a cardmember benefit of the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card. Cardmembers of the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass Card and The Hilton Honors American Express Business Card can also earn Diamond status through the end of the next calendar year if they spend $40,000 on eligible purchases on their card in a calendar year. You'll secure lifetime Hilton Diamond status once you've earned Hilton Diamond status for 10 years (the years don't need to be consecutive) and either stay 1,000 nights (paid and reward nights count) or spend $200,000 across your account's lifetime. Hilton Honors Diamond Reserve You'll earn Hilton Honors Diamond Reserve status after you stay 40 times or 80 nights and spend $18,000 in a calendar year. The primary benefits of Hilton Diamond Reserve status include: - A 120% bonus on base points earned through stays - 4 p.m. guaranteed late checkout - Premium club access, including access to the expanding collection of premium clubs - A confirmable upgrade reward, which lets you confirm a premium room upgrade (up to a suite) at the time of booking for a stay of up to seven nights Hilton status match and challenge Hilton Honors usually offers a status match and challenge to select elite members of other hotel loyalty programs. To request a Hilton Honors status match, you must submit proof of your status in another program via an online form. If Hilton approves your request, you'll get Hilton Gold status for 90 days. You can keep Gold status through March 31, 2028, if you stay for six nights during your 90-day trial period. Meanwhile, if you stay 12 nights within your 90-day trial period, Hilton will upgrade you to Diamond status through March 31, 2028. Related: Complete guide to airline status matches and challenges Milestone bonuses and status gifts Hilton offers its members several additional benefits based on the number of eligible nights they stay each calendar year. Once you stay 40 eligible nights in a calendar year, you'll get 10,000 bonus points. You'll then earn an additional 10,000 bonus points for every additional 10 eligible nights (up to 180) in a calendar year. Plus, you'll earn an additional 30,000 bonus points once you stay 60 eligible nights in a calendar year. And once you stay 120 eligible nights in a calendar year, you can choose a confirmable upgrade reward or 30,000 bonus points. If you stay 60 eligible nights in a calendar year, you can also gift Hilton Gold status to another member. And if you stay 100 eligible nights in a calendar year, you can gift Hilton Diamond status to another member. However, you can only gift status to one other member per year. Benefits for Hilton members at Small Luxury Hotels of the World properties You can book select Small Luxury Hotels of the World properties through Hilton Honors. Hilton Honors members get the following benefits when staying at participating SLH hotels: - Ability to earn Hilton points on stays (you can also redeem Hilton points for SLH stays) - Free Wi-Fi - Complimentary late checkout (subject to availability) Plus, Hilton Honors Gold members and above also enjoy: - Space-available room upgrades - Continental breakfast for you and up to one additional guest Related: The coolest SLH hotels you can book with Hilton Honors points Benefits for Hilton members on Explora Journeys You'll earn eligible nights, stays and spend toward Hilton Honors status on Explora Journeys. You'll also enjoy some extra perks based on your Hilton Honors tier as follows: - Member: 5% savings on all Journeys, a welcome gift and 5% savings on Journeys merchandise - Silver: Member benefits, plus a signature loyalty delight and dedicated customer support - Gold: Silver benefits, plus access to a cocktail event with ship leadership and a surprise gift or ritual - Diamond: Gold benefits, plus complimentary laundry service (one bag per Journey) and experience credits for destination experiences and ocean wellness - Diamond Reserve: Diamond benefits, plus complimentary laundry service (one bag per day), a behind-the-scenes bridge tour (upon availability) and a private transfer to the port How to earn Hilton points As you interact with the Hilton Honors program, you'll find many ways to earn points. For a detailed discussion, I highly recommend checking out our guide on earning Hilton points, but here's an overview of your options. Hotel stays One of the easiest ways to earn Hilton points is through hotel stays. On eligible stays, you'll usually earn as follows on charges to your folio from up to four rooms: - 3 points per dollar spent, plus 3,000 bonus points per 10 nights completed within the same stay, at LivSmart Studios properties - 5 points per dollar spent at Home2 Suites outside China, Homewood Suites, Spark, Tru, Yotel and Apartment Collection properties - 10 points per dollar spent at Home2 Suites in China and other Hilton brands Of course, as I mentioned above, you'll earn additional bonus points on stays if you have Hilton elite status. Plus, you may earn bonus points through current Hilton promotions. Related: 8 best Hilton all-inclusive resorts Hilton credit cards Hilton Amex cards are also a great way to earn points. Here's a look at the earning rates, welcome offers and annual fees on some of our favorite Hilton credit cards. | Card | Welcome offer | Earning rates | Annual fee | |---|---|---|---| | | Earn 200,000 bonus points after spending $6,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. | | | | | Earn 130,000 bonus points and a free night reward after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. | | | | | Earn 150,000 bonus points and a free night reward after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. | | | | | Earn 70,000 bonus points and a free night reward after spending $2,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. | | | I have the Hilton Aspire Card and find it offers far more value than its annual fee since I maximize its benefits. Plus, earning 14 points per dollar spent on purchases at Hilton properties is unbeatable. But if you don't maximize the annual free night reward and don't fully use the up to $400 Hilton resort statement credit (up to $200 statement credits biannually) each year, the Hilton Aspire may not be the right card for you. Related: Hilton Surpass vs. Hilton Aspire: Do you want Gold or Diamond status? Transfer rewards to Hilton You can also earn points by transferring rewards to Hilton Honors. Specifically, you can transfer American Express Membership Rewards points to Hilton Honors at a 1:2 ratio, meaning 1,000 Amex points could become 2,000 Hilton points. You can also transfer Bilt Points to Hilton Honors at a 1:1 ratio. You can usually get more value by transferring these points to other loyalty programs, so I wouldn't transfer my Amex or Bilt points to Hilton Honors. But even if you plan to transfer Amex or Bilt points to Hilton, it's usually a good idea to wait until you're ready to book your stay. Related: How (and why) you should earn transferable credit card points Hilton partners You can earn Hilton points when shopping or interacting with several partners. For example, you can earn points on eligible Alamo, Enterprise and National car rentals. You can also earn extra points at participating restaurants through the Hilton Honors Dining program and opt in to earn Hilton points on Lyft rides. Plus, you can earn Hilton points with Hilton's Vacation Ownership brand and on Explora Journeys. Hilton Honors event planner program Hilton Honors members can earn 2 points per dollar spent on guest rooms, meeting rooms and more (on up to $100,000 spent) through the Hilton Honors event planner program when holding a qualifying event at a participating Hilton property. Buy Hilton points Finally, you can buy Hilton points to boost your account balance. TPG's September 2026 valuations peg the value of Hilton points at 0.4 cents per point, and during the best sales, you can buy Hilton points for 0.5 cents each. So, you'll usually only want to buy Hilton points when doing so lets you book a high-value redemption. How to redeem Hilton points Just as there are many ways to earn Hilton points, there are plenty of ways to redeem your points. Check out our guide on redeeming Hilton points for all the details, but here's an overview of the best and worst ways to redeem Hilton points. Free night awards Hilton Honors doesn't publish an award chart and instead uses dynamic award pricing. However, there appears to be an unpublished cap on award pricing for each property, and standard award nights currently top out at 250,000 points at the most luxurious properties. If you want a good deal, consider using the Points Explorer tool to see point ranges at various properties over the next 30 days. Likewise, you can view monthly award pricing for a specific property by selecting "Shop by price" instead of stay dates. To get the best value when redeeming Hilton points, book an award stay for a standard room for five, 10, 15 or 20 nights. Assuming you have Hilton Silver status or higher, you'll get every fifth night free when redeeming points for stays of five nights or longer. Check TPG's current valuations and try to get at least our valuation of Hilton points on your redemption. Although you can redeem Hilton points for premium rooms, doing so will usually not provide good value. Related: 6 ways to maximize Hilton Honors redemptions Points & Money rewards You might want to book a Points & Money reward if you run short on points. This booking method lets you redeem any combination of points and cash for a stay. For example, here's one option for a stay that would otherwise cost 87,000 points or $367.13. You'll earn points on the money portion of Points & Money rewards stays at participating hotels. Pool or transfer Hilton points Hilton Honors is generous in allowing its members to pool and transfer points at no cost. You can pool or transfer points in increments of 1,000 points, up to 500,000. Each Hilton Honors member can send up to 500,000 points and receive up to 2 million points via combined pooling and transfer transactions each calendar year. However, each member can only make up to six transfers to other accounts and up to six points pooling transactions each calendar year. New Hilton Honors members can only pool, transfer or receive points 30 or more days after enrollment if they have account activity. Otherwise, they must wait at least 90 days after enrollment before pooling, transferring or receiving points without account activity. Hilton Honors Experiences Redeeming points for Hilton Honors Experiences has offered me strong value in the past. As such, I periodically check whether any experiences at my upcoming destinations are appealing. Be sure to check the paid rates, when available, before booking to determine whether redeeming points for the experience will provide good value. Related: How Hilton Honors points unlocked a premium NCAA basketball experience in Chicago Hilton Honors redemptions to avoid There are a few specific types of Hilton Honors redemptions that you'll want to avoid, as they offer extremely low value for your points. As you read through this section, keep in mind that TPG's September 2026 valuations pegged the value of Hilton points at 0.4 cents each. - Amazon Shop with Points: You can redeem 700 Hilton Honors points for a dollar of value at Amazon checkout, meaning you'll only get 0.14 cents per point. - Lyft credits: You can redeem 4,500 Hilton Honors points for a $10 Lyft credit, meaning you'd only get 0.22 cents per point. - Car rentals: A sample two-day Alamo car rental I priced out would cost $257.55 or 96,159 Hilton Honors points, meaning you'd only get 0.27 cents per point. - Transferring to airline miles: The transfer ratios usually make this a poor option unless you have no other use for Hilton points. I'd also add most premium-room reward nights to this list, as they usually offer a much lower cents-per-point redemption rate than standard-room rewards. Is Hilton Honors worth it? Hilton Honors is a popular program for a reason. Its main positives include the following: - Easy-to-earn status via credit cards - High earning rates on both card spending and hotel stays - A wide range of brands, including luxury, budget and extended stay - Large global footprint However, I personally find it difficult to get outsize value from Hilton Honors points. Hence, it isn't one of my primary hotel loyalty programs. Its negatives include: - Getting good value when redeeming Hilton points can be difficult. - Many elite benefits, even at higher tiers, are subject to availability and vary significantly by property. - Premium room reward pricing doesn't scale well, making it a poor redemption option in most cases. Despite these drawbacks, Hilton Honors can still be a very rewarding program, particularly if you can get elite status through a credit card and regularly stay at Hilton properties. Even if you don't stay with Hilton frequently, it's worth enrolling before your next stay to earn points and enjoy member benefits. For rates and fees of the Hilton Honors Amex, click here. For rates and fees of the Hilton Amex Aspire, click here. For rates and fees of the Hilton Surpass, click here. For rates and fees of the Hilton Business Amex, click here. Frequently asked questions Hilton Honors is Hilton's free hotel loyalty program. Once you join the program, you'll earn points on eligible stays at more than 9,000 properties worldwide that participate in Hilton Honors. Plus, you'll be able to redeem Hilton points for free nights and experiences. The program also offers elite status tiers that provide perks like bonus points and room upgrades. The fastest ways to earn Hilton Honors points are through hotel stays, Hilton cobranded credit cards and limited-time bonus point promotions. However, perhaps the quickest way to earn Hilton points is to simply purchase them. Hilton Honors elite status can provide meaningful value, especially for frequent travelers. Benefits may include bonus points on stays, complimentary breakfast or food-and-beverage credits at select brands, room upgrades and executive lounge access. However, benefits can vary widely by property, so the value of elite status depends heavily on how often and where you stay. You can earn Hilton Honors elite status by staying a required number of nights, completing a specific number of stays or meeting annual spending thresholds with Hilton. Hilton also offers shortcuts to elite status through select cobranded credit cards and status match opportunities for elite members of other hotel loyalty programs. Hilton Honors points are usually only worth buying during a promotion and when you have a specific redemption in mind. Since Hilton uses dynamic award pricing, buying points can occasionally help you book an expensive hotel stay for less than the cash rate. Yes. Hilton Honors points expire after 24 months of account inactivity. You must complete at least one stay at a Hilton property, earn points with a Hilton credit card, earn or redeem points with a Hilton partner, buy or donate points, or register for a Hilton promotion within 24 months to keep your Hilton Honors account active. Hilton Honors members with Silver status or higher receive every fifth night free on standard room reward stays booked entirely with points. The benefit applies automatically to eligible stays of five nights or longer, and you can get up to four free nights per reservation.

item.title: Chase Freedom Q4 categories: Up to 7% back on dining, grocery stores and American Red Cross donations
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.84
Chase Freedom Q4 categories: Up to 7% back on dining, grocery stores and American Red Cross donations Editor's Note If you have the Chase Freedom Flex® (see rates and fees) or legacy Chase Freedom®* in your wallet, the three rotating categories for Q4 have been announced. From Oct. 1 through Dec. 31, you'll earn up to 7% cash back (or up to 7 points per dollar spent) on dining, grocery stores and American Red Cross donations. You must activate your categories by Dec. 14 to earn at these rates (on up to $1,500 in combined spending across these categories; then 1% back or 1 point per dollar spent). Here's what you need to know about this quarter's categories. Last chance: Activate your Chase Freedom fourth-quarter categories *This card is no longer available to new applicants. The information for the Chase Freedom has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. Chase Freedom Q4 2026 categories From Oct. 1 through Dec. 31, Freedom and Freedom Flex cardholders will earn 5% cash back (or 5 points per dollar spent) across these bonus categories (on up to $1,500 in combined purchases; then 1% back or 1 point per dollar spent): - Dining (Freedom Flex cardholders will earn an elevated 7% cash back on these purchases for Q4) - Grocery stores - American Red Cross donations Dining already appeared as a bonus category earlier this year, so those who dine out often or order a lot of food delivery will appreciate a second chance to earn up to 7% cash back. Grocery stores are one of the most common quarterly bonus categories on the Freedom cards, while this is the first time we're seeing American Red Cross donations as a standalone category. And extra good news for Freedom Flex cardholders: the card will stop charging foreign transaction fees from Sept. 20, making it an excellent choice for dining and grocery purchases both in the U.S. and abroad in Q4. (We're unsure if legacy Freedom cardholders will enjoy the same privilege; check your Freedom card benefits guide in your online account after Sept. 20.) Activate this quarter's categories now to unlock their bonus-earning potential. You must activate by Dec. 14, but keep in mind that these categories will not go live until Oct. 1. It's simple to complete this process through your Chase account; just provide your last name, the last four digits of your card and your ZIP code. Analyzing the Q4 bonus categories The fourth quarter is a time when many people rack up plenty of charges from restaurants and grocery stores, between the holidays, end-of-year travel and gatherings with loved ones. Since dining and groceries are likely two of the highest spending categories for many Freedom cardholders, it's nice to see them offered as bonus categories at the same time. If you're feeling in a charitable mood this holiday season, consider using your eligible Freedom card to donate to the American Red Cross. Here are the details: - Dining: If you're a Freedom Flex cardholder, Chase has confirmed that you'll be eligible for a boosted 7% cash back on dining purchases, including eligible takeout and delivery; legacy Freedom cardholders (no longer open to applicants) will earn 5% cash back. 7% cash back is among the highest rates available for dining purchases, so Freedom Flex cardholders should make a point to charge those purchases — both in the U.S. and internationally — to that card in Q4. - Grocery stores: Whether you're buying weekly groceries, preparing for winter storms or gearing up for holiday meals, you'll be able to get 5% cash back on your grocery purchases with your eligible Freedom card. (Note that Walmart, Target, wholesale clubs, discount stores and some drugstores are not eligible for the quarterly bonus.) - American Red Cross donations: If you decide to donate to the American Red Cross in Q4, you'll earn 5% cash back on your donation. While some cards offer bonus rewards on charitable donations, it isn't too common. That makes your eligible Freedom card a great pick for any donations to this particular charity. Make sure to make your donation directly through the Red Cross, otherwise your purchase may not code correctly for the 5% bonus cash back. Remember that Chase limits the 5% cash back (or 5 points per dollar spent) you can earn to the first $1,500 spent in combined bonus categories each quarter. After you reach the maximum, you'll earn 1% back (or 1 point per dollar spent) on these purchases. Chase Freedom rotating categories history | Year | Quarter | Bonus categories | |---|---|---| | 2026 | Q4 | Dining (elevated 7% cash back for Freedom Flex cardholders), grocery stores and American Red Cross donations | | | Q3 | EV charging, gas stations, select live entertainment, transit and United Way | | | Q2 | Amazon, Chase Travel℠ (elevated 9% cash back for Freedom Flex cardholders), Feeding America and Whole Foods Market | | | Q1 | American Heart Association, dining (elevated 7% cash back for Freedom Flex cardholders) and Norwegian Cruise Line | | 2025 | Q4 | | | | Q3 | Gas and EV charging stations, Instacart and select live entertainment | | | Q2 | | | | Q1 | | | 2024 | Q4 | McDonald's (elevated 7% cash back for Freedom Flex cardholders), PayPal, pet shops and veterinarian services, and select charities | | | Q3 | Gas and EV charging stations, movie theaters and select live entertainment | | | Q2 | Hotels booked through Chase Travel, dining and Amazon (different earning rates depending on the card, i.e., 9%, 7% and 5%, respectively, for the Freedom Flex; 5% for all three categories for the Freedom) | | | Q1 | Select grocery stores, fitness club and gym memberships, and self-care and spa services | | 2023 | Q4 | PayPal, select charities and wholesale clubs | | | Q3 | Gas and EV charging stations, and select live entertainment | | | Q2 | Amazon and Lowe's | | | Q1 | Grocery stores, gym memberships and fitness clubs, and Target | | 2022 | Q4 | PayPal and Walmart | | | Q3 | Gas stations, rental cars, movie theaters and select live entertainment | | | Q2 | Amazon and select streaming services | | | Q1 | Grocery stores and eBay | | 2021 | Q4 | PayPal and Walmart | | | Q3 | Grocery stores and select streaming services | | | Q2 | Gas stations and home improvement stores | | | Q1 | Wholesale clubs, select streaming services and internet, cable and phone services | | 2020 | Q4 | PayPal and Walmart | | | Q3 | Amazon and Whole Foods Market | | | Q2 | Grocery stores, gym memberships and fitness clubs, and select streaming services | | | Q1 | Gas stations, internet, cable and phone services, and select streaming services | | 2019 | Q4 | Chase Pay, PayPal and department stores | | | Q3 | Gas stations and select streaming services | | | Q2 | Grocery stores and home improvement | | | Q1 | Gas stations, drugstores and tolls | | 2018 | Q4 | Wholesale clubs, department stores and Chase Pay | | | Q3 | Lyft, Walgreens and gas stations | | | Q2 | Groceries, PayPal and Chase Pay | | | Q1 | Mobile wallets, gas stations and internet, cable and phone service merchants | | 2017 | Q4 | Walmart and department stores | | | Q3 | Restaurants and movie theaters | | | Q2 | Grocery stores and drugstores | | | Q1 | Gas stations and local commuter transportation | | 2016 | Q4 | Wholesale clubs, drugstores and department stores | | | Q3 | Restaurants and wholesale clubs | | | Q2 | Grocery stores and wholesale clubs | | | Q1 | Gas stations and local commuter transportation | | 2015 | Q4 | Amazon, Zappos, Audible and Diapers.com | | | Q3 | Gas stations and Kohl's | | | Q2 | Restaurants, Bed Bath & Beyond, H&M and Overstock | | | Q1 | Grocery stores, movie theaters and Starbucks | | 2014 | Q4 | Amazon, Zappos and department stores | | | Q3 | Gas stations and Kohl's | | | Q2 | Restaurants and Lowe's | | | Q1 | Gas stations, movie theaters and Starbucks | Chase Freedom bonus categories FAQs How do rotating categories work? Each quarter, Chase announces a set of bonus categories that earn 5% cash back (or 5 points per dollar) for the next three months (on up to $1,500 in combined spending). Generally, these categories are announced halfway through the month before the new quarter starts, giving cardholders time to activate new categories. However, you can activate your categories until midway through the last month of the quarter. The categories tend to repeat periodically. For instance, grocery stores, restaurants and gas stations are all common categories you'll notice frequently pop up on the bonus calendar. So, depending on the categories and whether you can maximize them, these two cards can offer quite a nice chunk of cash back or bonus points over the year. How much cash back can I earn each quarter? Chase limits the 5% cash back (or 5 points per dollar) to the first $1,500 spent in combined bonus categories each quarter you activate the bonus. While that may not sound like a lot, that cash back adds up over time. Maximizing the cash-back categories each quarter, you'll earn $75 in cash back quarterly and up to $300 per year. For a no-annual-fee credit card, that's a lot of value. Alternatively, suppose you have a card that earns transferable Chase Ultimate Rewards points, like the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (see rates and fees). In that case, you can combine the rewards from your Chase Freedom or Freedom Flex card with those you earn from your more premium Ultimate Rewards-earning card. By doing this, your rewards become fully transferable. If you combine rewards this way, your $300 in bonus cash back would be worth 30,000 Ultimate Rewards points. TPG's September 2026 valuations peg Chase points at 2.05 cents apiece, making the 30,000 points you can earn in a year worth $615. How do I activate my 5% categories each quarter? You can head to Chase's site to activate your 5% cash back (or 5 points per dollar) categories for this quarter. You can also register through the Chase mobile app. Here's how to register: - Head to the Chase bonus activation page, or log in to your Chase account. - Enter your last name, the last four digits of your card number and your billing ZIP code. If you don't have your card on hand, log in to your Chase account to retrieve these digits. - Click "Activate your 5%" to register. - If you have multiple Chase Freedom cards, make sure to register each one. - Save a screenshot of your activation in case of any issues later, though you should also receive a "You're Activated!" confirmation email. Can I have both the Chase Freedom and the Chase Freedom Flex to double my earning potential? Yes, you can have both cards. So, if you already have the Chase Freedom and want to add the Chase Freedom Flex to your wallet, you're free to do so. Remember that the original Freedom card is no longer open to new applicants. If you'd rather only have one, though, the Freedom Flex is available as a product change. Of course, you'll also want to ensure you're eligible for a new Chase card. How do I maximize my Freedom and Freedom Flex cards? The most important thing is to activate your card to earn 5% cash back (or 5 points per dollar) each quarter in the specific categories and then use it for purchases in those categories. You can set up a recurring reminder in your calendar or sign up for the TPG newsletter. (We send out a reminder when it's time to activate every quarter, plus tips and tricks for how to maximize your card strategy and score some excellent award redemptions.) In addition to the rotating bonus categories, the Freedom Flex accrues 5% cash back on all other travel booked through Chase Travel, 3% cash back on drugstore purchases, 3% cash back on dining (including eligible delivery services) and 1% unlimited cash back on all other purchases. Better yet, when paired with a Chase credit card that earns fully transferable Ultimate Rewards points, such as the Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees) or the Chase Sapphire Preferred, the Chase Freedom Flex's 5% cash back effectively becomes 5 Ultimate Rewards points per dollar. You can learn all about this in our guide detailing the Chase Trifecta. Bottom line If you're a Chase Freedom or Freedom Flex cardholder, your Q4 categories include dining, grocery stores and American Red Cross donations. Most of these purchases will earn 5% cash back (or 5 points per dollar spent) from October through December. The exception is dining purchases on the Freedom Flex, which will earn an elevated 7% cash back (or 7 points per dollar spent). Activate these categories now so you don't miss out on any bonus rewards when these categories go live. And remember that Chase limits your quarterly bonus category earnings to the first $1,500 of combined spending each quarter. To learn more, read our full review of the Chase Freedom Flex. Apply here: Chase Freedom Flex TPG featured card | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent on purchases at restaurants worldwide, on up to $50,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent at US supermarkets, on up to $25,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 5X | Earn 5X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid hotel stays booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™. | | 3X | Earn 3X Membership Rewards® points on flights booked through AmexTravel.com, the Amex Travel App™, or purchased directly from airlines. | | 2X | Earn 2X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid car rentals booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™ and cruises booked and paid through AmexTravel.com. | | 1X | Earn 1X Membership Rewards® point per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases. |

item.title: Earn a first-year dollar-for-dollar cash-back match with these Discover offers
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.77
Earn a first-year dollar-for-dollar cash-back match with these Discover offers While they may not get as much fanfare as cards from giants like American Express and Chase, Discover cards are great choices for cash-back enthusiasts, beginner credit card users and simplicity-lovers alike. As Discover's cards migrate to Capital One's network, they're attracting fresh attention. If you've decided now is the right time to apply for a Discover card, make sure you know what offer you're getting. Discover doesn't typically change the welcome offers on its cards, so the answer to "When should I apply?" depends more on your personal situation than on the specific card's offer. Discover it Cash Back Best for: Those looking for flexible spending categories Current welcome offer: Receive an unlimited dollar-for-dollar cash-back match for your first cardholder year (no spending requirement). This is the standard offer for this card, so now is a good time to apply. Annual fee: $0 Key benefits: - 5% cash back in rotating quarterly categories (on up to $1,500 in combined spending each quarter; activation required) - 5% cash back on hotels, car rentals and attractions booked through Capital One Travel - 5% cash back on Capital One Entertainment purchases - 1% cash back on all other purchases - Access to Capital One Offers - Fraud protection and free credit score access To learn more, check out our full review of the Discover it® Cash Back. Apply here: Discover it® Cash Back Discover it Student Cash Back Best for: Students who want the highest welcome offer available from Discover Current welcome offer: Earn a $100 statement credit after spending $300 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. Plus, receive an unlimited dollar-for-dollar cash-back match for your first cardholder year (no spending requirement). Since this welcome offer lets you earn more than the standard first-year cash-back match, it's a great one to go for if you qualify. The statement credit portion of this offer is a limited-time offer, so don't wait to apply. Annual fee: $0 Key benefits: - 5% cash back in rotating quarterly categories (on up to $1,500 in combined spending each quarter; activation required) - 5% cash back on hotels, car rentals and attractions booked through Capital One Travel - 5% cash back on Capital One Entertainment purchases - 1% cash back on all other purchases - Access to Capital One Offers - No credit score required to apply - Fraud protection and free credit score access To learn more, check out our full review of the Discover it® Student Cash Back. Apply here: Discover it® Student Cash Back Discover it Miles Best for: Those who want to earn solid rewards on everyday purchases Current welcome offer: Receive an unlimited match on all miles you earn in your first cardholder year (no spending requirement). This is the same offer we've seen on this card for a long time, so we don't recommend waiting for a different one. Annual fee: $0 Key benefits: - 5 miles per dollar spent on hotels, car rentals and attractions booked through Capital One Travel - 5 miles per dollar spent on Capital One Entertainment purchases - 1.5 miles per dollar spent on all other purchases - Access to Capital One Offers - Fraud protection and free credit score access To learn more, check out our full review of the Discover it® Miles . Apply here: Discover it® Miles Discover it Chrome Best for: Those who spend a moderate amount on gas and dining and don't have another card that earns bonus rewards on these categories Current welcome offer: Receive an unlimited dollar-for-dollar cash-back match for your first cardholder year (no spending requirement). We don't expect this offer to change any time soon, so we recommend applying now. Annual fee: $0 Key benefits: - 5% cash back on hotels, car rentals and attractions booked through Capital One Travel - 5% cash back on Capital One Entertainment purchases - 2% cash back on gas stations and restaurants (on up to $1,000 in combined spending each quarter) - 1% cash back on all other purchases - Access to Capital One Offers - Fraud protection and free credit score access To learn more, check out our full review of the Discover it® Chrome. Apply here: Discover it® Chrome Discover it Student Chrome Best for: Students who spend a lot on gas and dining Current welcome offer: Receive an unlimited dollar-for-dollar cash-back match for your first cardholder year (no spending requirement). We don't expect this offer to change any time soon, so now is a great time to apply. Annual fee: $0 Key benefits: - 5% cash back on hotels, car rentals and attractions booked through Capital One Travel - 5% cash back on Capital One Entertainment purchases - 2% cash back on gas stations and restaurants (on up to $1,000 in combined spending each quarter) - 1% cash back on all other purchases - Access to Capital One Offers - Fraud protection and free credit score access Apply here: Discover it® Student Chrome Which Discover card is right for you? Discover's cards are geared toward cash-back fans and anyone looking to build or repair credit. While you won't find comprehensive travel benefits or merchant statement credits on any of their cards, that may be a welcome sight for some. Since all of Discover's cards have very similar perks, your choice will come down to which card's earning rates you prefer. If you're a student, you'll likely be best off with one of the issuer's student cards, since those should be the easiest to get approved for among the cards mentioned here. Who is eligible for a Discover card? As with any credit card, Discover may consider several factors when deciding whether to approve your application. These may include your credit score and previous history with the issuer. It's worth noting that Discover doesn't require a credit score for its two student cards, making either a great choice for those who are eligible. You'll need to be a student enrolled at least part-time at a college or university and be at least 18 years old to qualify. For any of its credit cards, Discover will require some form of income to get approved. If you're applying for one of its standard credit cards, expect a full-time job to be the requirement for approval. If you're applying for a student card, Discover states that a part-time job may qualify. If you're a student and you don't have a job right now, consider asking a family member to add you as an authorized user on their card. Otherwise, you'll need to wait until you have income to get your own credit card. Significant savings could also qualify you for a credit card, but keep in mind that you'll need a balance in the tens of thousands to make this a workable alternative. Bottom line If you're looking for a simple cash-back card to add to your wallet or you need a solid option for building credit, it's worth considering a Discover card. Since all Discover cards have no annual fee, they're easy to justify keeping over the long term. With all Discover products migrating over to Capital One's network, any Discover card you apply for now will be on Capital One's network. That means you'll enjoy additional benefits on your card, including access to Capital One Travel and Capital One Entertainment, as well as boosted earnings on these purchases through these two portals.

item.title: Capital One Venture Rewards current offer: 75,000 miles plus a $300 credit for Capital One Travel
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.64
Capital One Venture Rewards current offer: 75,000 miles plus a $300 credit for Capital One Travel Editor's Note The Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card is a great choice for beginners and experienced points-and-miles enthusiasts who want an easy way to earn miles with minimal effort — all for an affordable $95 annual fee. The Venture Rewards card's current welcome offer is especially compelling: Earn 75,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening. Plus, you'll receive a $300 credit upon approval to use on hotel and vacation rentals booked through Capital One Travel in the first cardholder year. Here's what the offer is worth and what to know before applying. Capital One Venture Rewards welcome offer New Capital One Venture Rewards cardholders can earn 75,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening. Plus, you'll receive a $300 credit upon approval to use on hotel and vacation rentals booked through Capital One Travel in the first cardholder year. Including the credit, this offer is worth $1,688, per TPG's September 2026 valuations. In terms of miles alone, this is the standard welcome bonus on the card. However, the inclusion of the $300 credit makes this offer among the most valuable we've seen. For comparison, previous welcome offers have gone as high as 100,000 miles after meeting the minimum spending requirements (no longer available), but with no credit. It's possible to squeeze even more from that bonus if you redeem Capital One miles for maximum value, thanks to their impressive roster of 15-plus transfer partners. Who is eligible for the Venture Rewards welcome bonus? There are some eligibility requirements to keep in mind before applying. You don't want to waste a hard pull on your credit report if you aren't eligible for the current offer. First, if you've previously earned a welcome bonus on the Venture Rewards, you won't be able to earn another one for 48 months. Note that this is 48 months from the date you received your bonus, not from the date you were approved. In addition, if you previously earned a welcome bonus on the Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card, you will more than likely not be eligible to earn a welcome bonus on the Venture Rewards. Capital One may consider multiple factors when deciding whether to approve you; for a deeper dive into its application requirements, check out our full guide. Related: The best Capital One credit cards Earning Capital One miles This card earns at least 2 miles per dollar spent on all purchases. So, by spending $4,000 on it to earn the welcome bonus, you'd earn at least 83,000 miles in the first few months, including the welcome bonus. And since the Venture Rewards earns 5 miles per dollar spent on car rentals, hotels and vacation rentals booked through Capital One Travel, it's possible to earn even more miles while working toward your welcome bonus. While some travel credit cards may earn slightly higher rates on select categories such as groceries or dining, the draw here is the simplicity and guarantee of earning at least 2 miles per dollar spent on anything you buy without the need to memorize multiple bonus spending categories. Related: Why I keep the Capital One Venture Rewards card in my wallet What can Capital One Miles get you? Your total value from this welcome bonus depends largely on how you redeem your miles. There are two key options: - Redeem for 1 cent apiece toward travel - Redeem by transferring to Capital One's 15-plus partner airlines and hotels (our recommendation) When converting your miles to hotel points or airline miles, most partners offer a 1:1 transfer ratio, though a couple of partners have different ratios. You can get great sweet spot redemptions by transferring miles to programs like Air Canada Aeroplan and Air France-KLM Flying Blue. For example, TPG's editor-in-chief, Nick Ewen, transferred 117,000 Capital One miles to Emirates Skywards to upgrade himself and two family members to Emirates first class. This broke down to 39,000 miles per person, a reasonable cost for the upgrade. If you don't want to transfer your miles, you can redeem them by booking a trip through Capital One Travel. These redemptions can be very handy in a world where you may be renting recreational vehicles, booking vacation home rentals or securing a cabin close to home more often than hopping on a flight to the other side of the world. Related: Cashing in Capital One miles? How to get the maximum value when redeeming miles Other Venture Rewards perks The Capital One Venture Rewards doesn't offer the same benefits as more premium travel rewards cards, including its upscale sibling, the Capital One Venture X Rewards. But for its modest $95 annual fee, the Venture Rewards provides some useful benefits: - An up to $120 statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck application fees - Car rental insurance - Complimentary concierge service - Extended warranty protection - No foreign transaction fees Related: Chase Sapphire Preferred Card vs. Capital One Venture Rewards Bottom line The Capital One Venture Rewards remains a strong option for travelers who value simplicity. It earns at least 2 miles per dollar spent on purchases and gives cardholders access to Capital One's airline and hotel transfer partners, all for a $95 annual fee. Plus, the current welcome offer includes a solid haul of miles and a $300 credit for Capital One Travel, one of the best offers we've seen. Just remember to use your credit in the first cardholder year, or you'll forfeit the value. To learn more, read our full review of the Capital One Venture Rewards card. Learn more: Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card For Capital One products listed on this page, some of the benefits may be provided by Visa® or Mastercard® and may vary by product. See the respective Guide to Benefits for details, as terms and exclusions apply.

item.title: These are North America's best airports, according to JD Power's 2026 rankings
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.62
These are North America's best airports, according to JD Power's 2026 rankings Travelers continue to be fed up with expensive airfare, crowded lounges and full flights, but there's a huge bright spot in the travel experience: the airport. That's according to research from J.D. Power, which released its annual North America airport satisfaction study on Wednesday. The results broadly followed the same trends as last year, with overall satisfaction scores continuing to increase. The study is the latest evidence of a powerful trend that has seen U.S. airports — including those once derided as "third-world" by then-Vice President Joe Biden — undergo drastic transformations into terminals perfectly designed to serve modern passengers, including both frequent flyers and occasional travelers. Related: Washington, DC's Reagan National Airport plans $800 million expansion For the study, J.D. Power divided airports into three categories: "Mega" airports see 33 million or more passengers per year. "Large" airports are transited by 10 million to 32.9 million passengers each year. And "medium" airports serve 4.5 million to 9.9 million passengers annually. The study ranks airports in each category on a scale of 1,000 points. Notably, the average score in each segment was higher than in 2025, which in turn had climbed significantly from 2024. Every category of airport improved even higher than 2025 Customer satisfaction with mega airports was an average of 14 points higher in 2026 compared to the previous year, while large airports gained 13 points and medium airports improved by 16 points. In 2026, Minneapolis-Saint Paul International Airport (MSP) led the mega category, mirroring results from the past two years. The airport scored 684 points. Tampa International Airport (TPA) led large airports with 715 points, and Charleston International Airport (CHS) was the top-performing medium airport with 712 points. In the "mega" category, MSP was followed by Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport (DTW) with 663 points and Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) with 642 points. Portland International Airport (PDX) ranked second among large airports with 708 points, while Dallas Love Field (DAL) followed in third place with a score of 698. Ontario International Airport (ONT) in California was the runner-up among medium airports with 705 points, while Indianapolis International Airport (IND) — which has led the category for the last four years — ranked third with a score of 695. You can see the full results at the bottom of this story. Related: New York JFK's $19B rebuild: The giant, new Terminal One is just a year away The results are based on surveys of 24,710 U.S. or Canadian residents who had traveled through at least one U.S. or Canadian airport within the past 30 days. The survey was fielded between July 2025 and July 2026. It focused on seven key factors: - Ease of travel through the airport - Level of trust in the airport - Terminal facilities - Airport staff - Food and retail experience - Experience departing from or arriving at the airport via plane - Experience arriving at or departing from the airport via ground transport What's behind increasing satisfaction with North American airports? The improving experience at North American airports is largely the result of various construction projects completed over the past few years, ranging from brand-new terminal buildings and expansions to runway repairs, which have led to fewer delays. "For the better part of the last decade, nearly every airport, from the largest international hubs to midsized airfields, has undertaken a significant capital improvement project aimed at streamlining passenger flow, adding attractive food and beverage options and improving overall passenger experience," Michael Taylor, J.D. Power's managing director of travel, hospitality and retail, said in a statement. "On the whole, those efforts are finally starting to pay off in the form of higher overall passenger satisfaction scores," Taylor added. "However, when it comes to the individual experiences of passengers, every detail counts and the specific design and structural decisions airports make can have a significant influence on how passengers spend their time — and their money — in the terminal." Related: Chicago O'Hare is a huge construction site — here's what's going up Notably, all of the highest-ranked airports in the study have either recently completed or are nearing completion of extended capital improvement projects, J.D. Power noted. Many of those projects have included major transformations of the food, beverage and retail options in the terminals, giving passengers more options for where to eat or shop before a flight. While many of those improvements have included bringing local color to the airports, finding the right balance with major national chains led to the highest scores, the report found. Or as Taylor put it during the release of last year's report: "A decades-long trend of bringing unique, local flavor to the passenger experience has positively impacted the airport experience with these local touches having a major influence on passenger satisfaction." Below is the full list of airport ratings. Mega airports These are the best-rated mega airports in North America for 2026, according to J.D. Power. Large airports These are the best-rated large airports in North America for 2026, according to J.D. Power. Medium airports These are the best-rated medium airports in North America for 2026, according to J.D. Power.

item.title: American's next premium plans: Way more Flagship Suites, new (and improved) lounges
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.43
American's next premium plans: Way more Flagship Suites, new (and improved) lounges It's about to get a lot easier to book a flight featuring one of American Airlines' fancy new Flagship Suites. With brand-new planes coming and older ones getting makeovers, the the posh new business-class product will be on many more aircraft in the coming months — and years. American debuted its next-generation suites last year to plenty of fanfare. It was the airline's first premium seat with sliding privacy doors. But until now, you had to be pretty savvy to actually score a flight featuring the new suites. As of today, AA's Flagship seats are only available on a small portion of its fleet: - A handful of brand-new Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners - A few long-range, single-aisle Airbus A321XLRs - Plus, one Boeing 777-300ER that just got a total on-board makeover with the new seats. But there are a lot more planes still to come. Older planes to get new cabin (and suites) American has announced its new flagship cabin will get installed on nearly its entire long-haul fleet over the next few years. In fact, as it stands today there's only one type of twin-aisle jet American hasn't slated for a refresh: its Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners that got delivered prior to 2025. It begs the question: Could those jets also get Flagship Suites eventually? "It's an active debate," Rhonda Crawford, American's senior vice president of customer experience and design, told me earlier this month, adding: "I would just say everything's on the table right now." American essentially has two types of 787-9s flying today. The newest planes seat 244 passengers and include the premium-heavy layout that features 51 of the Flagship Suites that debuted last year. The airline also has a 285-seat legacy configuration that dates back as far as the mid-2010s. It's worth watching how AA handles its Dreamliner fleet in the coming years. Regardless, international flying on American will certainly look a lot different by the end of this decade with a refresh to nearly all the planes it uses for long-haul service. Narrowbody planes set for upgrade, too By the way: American's single-aisle planes are slated for a big makeover, too. Last month, the carrier announced it would bring back seatback screens and outfit those jets with more first-class and extra legroom seats. That rollout is set to begin in 2028. 'First quarter' of a lounge glow-up Meanwhile, American has also been busy making major announcements about its plans on the ground. After promising a "steady stream" of airport lounge news late last year, the carrier has followed through. American has revealed new or significantly expanded clubs in Austin, Charlotte, Chicago, Dallas, Nashville, New York and Washington. On top of that, the airline has been upgrading the food it serves in its outposts. Apparently, American isn't done yet. "We are in the beginning quarter," Crawford said of the carrier's lounge plans. "There's more to come, and there's more in the pipeline, for sure," she added. "Lots of opportunity for refurbs and rebuilds, and expansions, and restorations, and all of the above." Provisions plans I wouldn't be surprised if you saw more of AA's newest lounge concept called Provisions by Admirals Club. That's the new permanent grab-and-go lounge setup the airline debuted last summer at Charlotte Douglas International Airport (CLT). Since then, American has announced additional Provisions locations for John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) and Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW). American's inaugural CLT Provisions location was more functional in nature. But it appears the carrier has more elaborate planes for its JFK and DFW locations — including a full-service coffee bar in New York. "You'll see us continue to optimize and hone in [on] those and improve those," Crawford said. Grab-and-go lounge locations can be a helpful way for airlines to reduce crowding in their main clubs. Those outposts allow members who only need a cup of coffee and a quick bite to eat to briefly stop in, grab what they need, and leave without occupying seats. Related reading:

item.title: Citi / AAdvantage Executive statement credits: What they are and how to use them
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.18
Citi / AAdvantage Executive statement credits: What they are and how to use them Editor's Note The Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (see rates and fees) is American Airlines' premium cobranded credit card with Citi, best known for its complimentary Admirals Club membership. Following a recent refresh, the card also offers a collection of statement credits that can help offset its $695 annual fee. These include credits for American Airlines Vacations, inflight and Admirals Club purchases, Avis and Budget rentals and Global Entry or TSA PreCheck application fees. Here's a closer look at each of the Citi / AAdvantage Executive's statement credits and how to use them. Overview of Citi / AAdvantage Executive credits The Citi / AA Executive Mastercard offers five statement credits covering expenses ranging from American Airlines travel and inflight purchases to rental cars and ride-hailing services. | Credit | Value | |---|---| | American Airlines Vacation Credit | Up to $500 annually; split into two periods (January to June and July to December) | | Inflight and Admirals Club purchases | Up to $100 per calendar year | | Avis/Budget | Up to $120 per calendar year | | Global Entry/TSA PreCheck | Up to $120 every four years | | Lyft | Up to $180 annually; $15 per month (after taking three eligible rides in a calendar month) | Related: Is the Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard worth it? American Airlines Vacations credit The Citi / AA Executive Mastercard offers up to $500 in American Airlines Vacations statement credits each calendar year. The benefit is split into two six-month periods: up to $250 from Jan. 1 through June 30, and another up to $250 from July 1 through Dec. 31. To qualify, you'll need to book an eligible American Airlines Vacations travel package or experience through AAVacations.com and pay with your Citi / AA Executive card. This isn't a general American Airlines travel credit, so standalone airfare booked through AA.com won't qualify. If you can naturally use the full $500 annual benefit, it can offset a substantial portion of the card's $695 annual fee. But the value you actually get from this credit also depends on how American Airlines Vacations package pricing compares with booking your trip separately. When I priced a three-night trip for two from Dallas to Las Vegas, an American Airlines Vacations package with roundtrip American Airlines flights and a stay at the Bellagio cost $2,473. Booking the same flights directly with American cost $1,086, while booking the same room directly with the Bellagio cost $1,595, for a total of $2,681. In this case, the vacation package was already $208 cheaper than booking the components separately. After factoring in the card's $250 statement credit, the effective package cost dropped to $2,223 — a savings of $458 compared with booking separately. Package pricing can vary, though, so I'd still compare the cost of booking through American Airlines Vacations with booking each component separately before using the credit. Inflight and Admirals Club purchase credit The Citi / AA Executive Mastercard offers up to $100 in statement credits each calendar year on eligible American Airlines inflight and Admirals Club purchases. Eligible purchases can include food and beverages purchased onboard American Airlines flights, as well as eligible purchases at Admirals Club locations. While Admirals Clubs offer complimentary food and select drinks, you may encounter additional charges for premium beverages, such as cocktails or higher-end wines. For cardholders who regularly fly American, this is the card's easiest statement credit to use. Eligible purchases charged to your card will receive statement credits until you've reached the $100 annual maximum, so you don't have to keep track of a monthly or quarterly allotment. (It's also worth noting that some existing cardholders can temporarily stack this credit with the card's outgoing 25% discount on eligible inflight food and beverage purchases. Cardholders who applied before Aug. 23, 2026, will retain that benefit through Sept. 30, 2026; new cardholders don't receive the 25% discount.) Related: The Citi / AAdvantage Executive's new benefits are live: 6 things to do now Avis and Budget prepaid rental credit Citi / AA Executive cardholders can receive up to $120 in statement credits each calendar year on eligible prepaid Avis and Budget car rentals booked directly through Avis.com or Budget.com. This benefit can be useful if you rent cars at least occasionally, since a single rental could potentially use up much or all of the annual credit. However, you'll need to actively keep track of the requirements: The rental must be prepaid and booked directly with Avis or Budget to qualify, so bookings through third-party sites, travel agencies or other channels — including AA.com/cars — won't trigger the credit. This narrow eligibility window is where some cardholders run into trouble. The prepaid booking requirement itself carries an additional limitation: a $50 cancellation penalty if you cancel more than 24 hours before pickup or $150 if you cancel within 24 hours. If your travel plans are uncertain, those fees could easily erode the value of a $120 credit. I'd also compare prepaid Avis and Budget rates with other available rental options rather than booking with either company solely to use the credit. Saving $120 isn't particularly valuable if you're paying substantially more for the rental in the first place, especially given the risk of prepaid cancellation. Primary cardholders can also enroll for complimentary Avis President's Club status (through Aug. 31, 2028). The status includes perks such as upgrades (where available) and guaranteed availability up to a full-size car (with a confirmed reservation at least 24 hours in advance). These benefits — combined with the prepaid rental credit — can offset the inconvenience of booking directly, particularly for cardholders who rent regularly. Global Entry/TSA PreCheck credit The Citi / AA Executive Mastercard provides up to $120 in statement credits every four years toward a Global Entry or TSA PreCheck application fee. Eligible application fees charged to the card will receive a statement credit of up to $120. If you're choosing between the two programs, Global Entry is the better option for international travelers because it includes TSA PreCheck. If you already have a membership, you can use the credit to cover an eligible application fee for a friend or family member instead. Related: The best credit cards for Global Entry and TSA PreCheck Lyft credit The Citi / AA Executive Mastercard offers up to $180 in Lyft credits annually, but maximizing this benefit requires quite a lot of effort. You must complete three eligible Lyft rides in a calendar month before receiving $15 in credits for that month, and you'll need to meet that requirement every month to receive the full annual value. That makes this credit most useful for regular, committed Lyft users who already take at least three rides each month. If your Lyft use is more sporadic, I wouldn't place much value on this benefit, since taking extra rides solely to unlock a $15 credit is unlikely to make financial sense. If you can use the benefit naturally, make sure your Citi / AAdvantage Executive is linked to your account and keep the three-ride threshold in mind each month. Grubhub credit (only available to some existing cardholders) An up to $10 monthly credit for eligible Grubhub purchases is being phased out. Cardholders who applied for their Executive card before Aug. 23, 2026, receive the credit through Aug. 31, 2027; new cardholders don't. Bottom line The Citi / AAdvantage Executive offers a suite of statement credits that are best suited to American Airlines loyalists who can take advantage of the card's travel-focused benefits. The inflight and Global Entry credits are the easiest to use, while the AA Vacations and car rental credits require you to do some research. The Lyft credit is the hardest to get value from.
